HONDA CRV OWNER'S MANUAL  -  WELCOME AND DRIVING (1 of 3)

WELCOME TO YOUR CRV
Thank you for choosing Honda. Your CRV drives like a car on the highway and keeps going when the road gives out: Real Time 4WD sends power to the rear wheels the moment the front ones slip. Inside it is more practical than it looks: the rear seats fold into a flat floor and a bed, the cargo floor lifts out as a picnic table, and under it is a storage well. Four seats, a 2.0-litre twin-cam engine, regular fuel, 58 litres in the tank with the filler on the left. Read this manual once, front to back: a mechanic who has read it learns more from every part fitted, removed or repaired on a CRV. Keep it in the glove box.

DRIVING
Most of the time your CRV drives its front wheels. On ice, mud or loose gravel, the rear wheels join in by themselves, within moments, and let go again when grip comes back: no lever, nothing to engage. Paved roads, gravel, dirt tracks, fields and snow are home ground; rocks and deep mud are not. Slow down off the pavement: the springs are soft and the tyres are road tyres. Look after the timing belt: if it breaks, the engine is ruined. A full roof and armour make the car slower to stop, so brake early.
Print_Text_CRVGen1_Manual2_info:
HONDA CRV OWNER'S MANUAL  -  LOAD SPACE (2 of 3)

REAR SEATS AND A NIGHT IN THE CAR
Fold the seatbacks down and tumble the seats: the back of the cabin becomes one long, flat floor, about twice the cargo area, or, made up as a bed, a far better bed than any back seat. Both rear seats must be in the car and empty, and nobody can sit in the back while they are folded; clear the floor before you put them back up. For a night in the car: fold the seats before dark, lock up with the windows up, take the picnic table out for supper and put it back before you drive on, and keep a full jerry can for the morning. The full-size spare rides on the back; a jack and a lug wrench change a wheel.

PICNIC TABLE, STORAGE WELL, ROOF
Open the tailgate and lift the cargo floor: under it is a well for the things you would rather keep out of sight, and once you know it is there it is yours to use. The floor panel has folding legs: take it out, set it up as a table wherever you stop, and put it back before you drive on. The roof rack takes up to 50 kg, strapped down where everyone can see it. Two jerry cans fit, one on the spare and one on the rack, and they hold real fuel.
Print_Text_CRVGen1_Manual3_info:
HONDA CRV OWNER'S MANUAL  -  ACCESSORIES AND MODIFICATIONS (3 of 3)

ACCESSORIES AND MODIFICATIONS
From your dealer: the bull bar and the roof rack bolt on with a wrench, the windshield, window and rear glass guards with a screwdriver, the spare tire cover by hand. Aftermarket: a snorkel, a steel skid plate, a rear steel bumper with a hitch, a roof ladder and jerry cans, each bolted on and off again. The Kestrel Trail Claw 3-inch lift puts the car on 30-inch all-terrain tyres, on the EX alloys or on black steel wheels; fitting it takes a jack, a lug wrench, a wrench and an experienced mechanic, with the engine off and everyone out, and the kit comes back if you take it off. The plans are in "4x4 Off-Road: CRV Edition".

NOTES IN THE BACK OF THE MANUAL
Taped in from "Survival Armour": door plates, window mesh, wheel arch guards and a rear glass plate, welded at a workbench and bolted on with a wrench and a screwdriver. Armoured windows stay shut, and nothing gets an arm in. The steel wears down as it takes the hits, and every plate makes the car heavier. In pen: plates done at Al's in October; check them after every run. Glove box lid sticks: lift it and pull. Slept in it three nights at the lake. Storage well: spare keys, flashlight, the good tape.
